description:
Maintainer, 2026-08-04: 'the turbine blades are reaction + impulse. They are angled differently at each stage. Have placeholder angles for those. When detailed turbine design lands (and it should later), then take the angulation from the physical turbine model.'

INTERIM (done under op-wqk.14.3): stator + rotor blades are drawn with a PLACEHOLDER per-stage angle schedule. These are illustrative only and MUST be labelled as such in the doc comments -- they are not derived from any turbine design and must never be presented as if they were.

THE PHYSICS THEY STAND IN FOR:
  - Degree of reaction is the fraction of the stage enthalpy drop taken across the ROTOR. Impulse ~ 0% (all expansion in the fixed nozzle/stator, rotor just turns the flow); reaction typically ~50% (expansion split between stator and rotor).
  - Classic steam-turbine practice puts impulse stages at the HP inlet (Rateau/Curtis) and reaction stages toward the LP exhaust (Parsons), so a multi-stage machine is a MIXTURE and the blade angles vary stage by stage -- which is exactly why one fixed angle for all rows is wrong.
  - The blade SHAPES differ too, not just the angles: impulse rotor blades are near-symmetric buckets; reaction blades are asymmetric aerofoils. If the drawing is to distinguish stage types honestly, shape should follow angle.

WHEN THIS IS DONE: the angles must come from the real turbine model rather than the placeholder schedule -- stator exit angle alpha and rotor inlet/outlet angles beta per stage, plus the degree of reaction per stage. That model does not exist yet; it arrives with the detailed turbine design work (see op-dt3.18, the TampinesSteamArray-coupled turbine). Wire the dependency and delete the placeholder schedule at that point; do not leave both paths live.
title: TurbineVisual: per-stage blade angulation from the physical turbine model (replace placeholders)
